claims.text: The E11 write-scope gate predicate in ARM-08's RxCounterAuthority.cpp (origin/arm/e11-authority-impl-v1 @ 08f742a) is CORRECT: compiled standalone with g++ -std=c++17 and called directly, it passes 18/18 assertions derived from RX_SKILL_ENUMS_V1.md 4.0/4.1 — boss_stability is refused as RejectAuthorityOwned, boss_release_delay is admitted, unknown/empty/nullptr and prefix/suffix/truncation/case/space attacks are all refused as RejectUnknownCounter, the two rejection reasons stay distinguishable, and exactly one of six registry rows is A2-writable.

That 18/18 result is discriminating, not vacuous: seven mutations applied to the PRODUCT translation unit (never the harness) were every one detected, each producing a DISTINCT failure signature, while the unmutated TU fired zero assertions. The harness localises which defect was introduced rather than merely alarming that something broke.

The gate is UNREACHABLE from the player-facing path. FRxSimWorld::ParseSkillSpec (RxSimWorld.cpp:158, called from author_skill at :930) reads exactly six fields — name, trigger, effect, cost, cooldown, commit_window — and never touches `effects`, so FRxSkillSpec::Effects is always empty and the gate loop at RxSkillSystem.cpp:217 iterates nothing. boss_stability is safe today because the parser cannot express the attack, not because the gate refuses it: UNREACHABLE, not GATED.

The absence of any writer to FRxSkillSpec::Effects is claimed against a named search surface: FRxSkillEffect (RxSkillSystem.h:86) is a plain C++ struct and not a USTRUCT, so no reflection-based deserialiser can populate it without naming it; git grep across all of Source/** for `.Effects`, `Effects.Add|Emplace|Num` and `FRxSkillEffect` returns three hits — two declarations and one read — and no writer.

The reachability verdict is itself discriminating on the same causal path: four scratch trees produce four DISTINCT exit codes — R0 as-shipped exits 3 (correct but unreachable), R1 with ParseSkillSpec populating Effects exits 0 (GATE LIVE), R2 reachable plus boss_stability made writable exits 1 (BREACH), R3 with the gate source removed exits 2 (cannot evaluate). R1 proves the check can recognise a live correct gate and not only condemn an unreachable one; R2 proves reachability alone is not read as safety.

One registry cite is stale: RxCounterAuthority.cpp cites FRxBossEarthquake::TremorStage at RxBossEarthquake.h:81, but line 81 is blank and the field is at :80. ARM-08's check_registry_matches_doc.py cannot catch this class of drift because it parses the writability column only and never examines the cite string. Severity is documentation — it changes no admission decision.

A suspected functional defect is FALSIFIED. The stale NOTE at RxSkillSystem.cpp:238-240 states that AuthorSkill maps any validation failure to ERR_STATE, which would flatten the gate's ERR_AUTHORITY at the player-facing boundary. The code at :268-273 in fact propagates the code explicitly so ERR_AUTHORITY survives. The comment is stale and contradicts the code 30 lines below it; the functional defect does not exist.

The cite check published above was wrong on its first run and was corrected before publication: it reported TremorStage 'is at :64' because RxBossEarthquake.h declares int32 TremorStage twice — at :64 in FRxBossSnapshot and at :80 in FRxBossEarthquake — and the check matched the bare field name while ignoring the Type:: qualifier it had already parsed. Right about the failure, wrong about the diagnosis. Fixed by scoping the search to the qualifier's declaration span.

The prior blocker 'K-01C behavioural half needs a built editor carrying ARM-08's code' is retired for the gate predicate and its reachability. ARM-08 wrote RxCounterAuthority as a deliberately UE-free translation unit precisely so it could be linked by a host-toolchain test without an engine build. A built editor is still required to exercise the gate inside a running sim, which this checkpoint does not do.

decisions_requested: ARM-08's gate is correct and not load-bearing. Whether to wire FRxSimWorld::ParseSkillSpec to read an `effects` array is a product decision above L2 — it changes what a player-authored spec can express. ARM-06 recommends it be decided explicitly rather than left implicit, because the current state reads as 'gated' to anyone who greps for the gate.

Silent drop: a spec carrying an `effects` array today validates OK and the effects vanish with no diagnostic. If wiring the parser is deferred, ARM-06 recommends ParseSkillSpec reject an unrecognised `effects` key rather than ignore it, so the no-op is visible. This is a change to ARM-08's file and is not in ARM-06's writable scope.

The stale cite (RxBossEarthquake.h:81 -> :80) is in ARM-08's RxCounterAuthority.cpp and in ARM-08's copy of RX_SKILL_ENUMS_V1.md. ARM-06's copy already carries the correction, so this will surface as merge drift. Routing to ARM-08 rather than fixing it across a scope boundary.
risks: C1 and C2 verify the predicate as a standalone C++ function compiled by g++ 13.3.0. The shipped artifact is compiled by UE's toolchain with different flags and a different standard library. Nothing here proves the predicate behaves identically in an editor build, only that the source is correct as written.

The reachability finding is a static claim about a hand-written parser. It is strong — FRxSkillEffect is not a USTRUCT, so reflection is excluded, and no writer exists in Source/** — but it is still text analysis, not execution. A writer introduced through a path this scan does not model would falsify C3, and the test would need to be re-run to catch it.

test_e11_cxx_gate.py reads its subject from origin/arm/e11-authority-impl-v1 when the worktree lacks the file. That ref is a moving target: ARM-08 pushing a new commit changes what this test exercises without any change to ARM-06's tree. The provenance file pins the sha exercised at this checkpoint (08f742a); a later run proving something different is expected, not a contradiction.

Exit 3 (UNEXERCISED) remains a new code in this fleet's test vocabulary. Any external runner treating non-zero as failure reads 'correct but not load-bearing' as a defect. Restated from CHECKPOINT-41 because a second test now emits it.
ARM-06 has 33 commits unpushed. Every artifact in this checkpoint exists only in one worktree.
